authoredNote: Written from the M60/S1 owner model; spellings and lines recorded from the post-fix run. The scope rule is a SUPPRESSION rule, so `forbidRelationships` carries most of the assertion: 14 of the 31 pinned rows are rows that must NOT be published. A symbol constraint is matched field-for-field against the published symbol object, which carries `range` and not `line`, so no expectSymbols row may use `line` — the line is pinned on the RELATIONSHIP instead, where line_number is a real constraint. Relationship rows do carry line_number.
rationale: M60/S1 — the whole `contains` model in one file, because the label's correctness is a conjunction and each conjunct had been broken independently. OWNER: a member belongs to its NEAREST enclosing owner, and an owner is a type (class/object/trait/enum), a method, a `given`, or an anonymous class. A val is not an owner; neither is an `extension`. SCOPE: a `val`/`var` inside a FUNCTION SCOPE — a method OR a LAMBDA — is not extracted, and the scope is cleared by the next type, `given`-independent, or anonymous class. The lambda clause is what the previous oracle missed: a val's nearest OWNER can be a class while a lambda still gates it, and that was all 56 of cats-effect's unexplained test-suite rows (`ticked("..") { implicit t => val r0 = ... }` parses as block > lambda_expression > val_definition). NAME: read the `name:` FIELD, never the first identifier child — the latter published `Names contains x`, a method's parameter. Measured: MISSING=0 and UNEXPLAINED=0 on all 457 cats-effect files and a 400-file scala3 draw (23,081 truth edges).
